messages.subject: fitPLM
parts:
Dear list,

in the affyPLM package, the function fitPLM() does background
correction, quantile normalisation and probelevel model fitting under
the same command.

Working under aroma.affymetrix, does the function RmaPlm() work
similarly or should I do the three steps separately?

By the way, after having fit a model, I can get a NUSE plot using
plotNuse() function, but is there a function that gets the actual
median NUSE values for each chip? or are the NUSE values stored
anywere after fitting the model?

Thanks,

David

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] fitPLM
parts:
Hi David.

You'll have to do the steps separately.

I'm not sure what everyone else in the list does, but I created a
wrapper function (see below 'doEverything') that does the background
adjustment, normalization and plm fitting, all in one go (and I have
options to do exon array analysis). It might be useful to others.
Basically, you tell it the name of the dataset and the chip type and
that is all it needs to know to trace your directory structure and
find everything it needs. It returns a list of all the things you
might need (chip effects, quality assessment model, etc.). For
example, you might do something like to do the quality assessment:

e<-doEverything("my_dataset","HG-U133_Plus_2")
plotNuse(e$qam)

The nice thing about this is that if you've already processed the
data once, it'll whip through all these steps. However, you can make
it recalculate everything by setting force=T.

As for the actual NUSE calculations, I think you can call it as 'n<-
plotNuse(e$qam)' to get the values (though I've never done this).
Otherwise, you might check the code in
'plotNuse.QualityAssessmentModel'.

Hope that works.
Mark

doEverything<-function
(name,chip,checkChipType=F,doExon=F,doCore=F,force=F,doMerge=F,doResidua
ls=F,doWeights=F,getExpression=F,verbose=Arguments$getVerbose(-8)) {
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chip,
checkChipType=checkChipType)
if (doCore)
chip<-paste(chip,",core",sep="")
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chip)
setCdf(cs, cdf)
bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)
csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose,force=force)
setCdf(csBC, cdf)
qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose,force=force) #time required
setCdf(csN, cdf)
if (doExon)
plm <- ExonRmaPlm(csN,mergeGroups=doMerge)
else
plm <- RmaPlm(csN)
fit(plm, verbose=verbose,units=NULL) #time required
qam <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm)
chp<-getChipEffectSet(plm)
d<-NULL; ws<-NULL; rs<-NULL
if (getExpression) {
if (!doExon | doMerge)
d<-getExprs(chp,doExon=F)
else
d<-getExprs(chp,doExon=T)
}
if (doResiduals)
rs<-calculateResiduals(plm,verbose=verbose,force=force)
if (doWeights)
ws<-calculateWeights(plm,verbose=verbose,force=force)
list
(name=name,chip=chip,d=d,cs=csN,cdf=cdf,plm=plm,qam=qam,chp=chp,res=rs,w
ts=ws)
}

getExprs <- function(ces,doExon=F, ...) {
cdf <- getCdf(ces);
theta <- extractMatrix(ces, ..., returnUgcMap=TRUE);
ugcMap <- attr(theta, "unitGroupCellMap");
if (doExon) {
x<-getFile(ces,1)
y<-readUnits(x)
cn<-names(unlist(y,recursive=F))
rownames(theta) <-cn
} else {
un<-getUnitNames(cdf, ugcMap[,"unit"]);
rownames(theta) <- un
}
log2(theta)

}
